Yes. The appellate court is likely to reverse: zoning compliance is not an absolute right to site a house so that it destroys a neighbor’s preexisting solar use, and private-nuisance balancing can treat that interference as unreasonable when an alternative placement would avoid the harm. Blocking sunlight is not a substantive-due-process violation, and these facts do not show that a comparative weighing favors the neighbor.
CONFIDENCE: 72
